```{r setup}
#| message: false
#| error: false
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(viridis)
library(glmmTMB)
library(lme4)
library(car)
library(performance)
library(ggeffects)

dat <- read.csv('Fiddler_cages_marsh_stability_working.csv') 
summary(dat)

ss_dat <- read.csv('Fiddler_cages_soil_strength_2026_working.csv')

sed_dat <- read.csv('Sediment_deposition_working.csv')
```

Before making graphs I need to do some calculations.
Each site there were 3 replicates of sediment deposition tubes to get a mean of sediment deposition.
So I need to calculate the mean than find the deposition rate per area per time so I can compare it across sites.
```{r mean}

sed_dat <- sed_dat %>%
  group_by(Site_ID)%>%
  summarise(
    sed_av = mean(Value), #sediment deposition is in long format already and g/cm2/day format per replicate
    sed_sd = sd(Value)
  )

```

Currently, mussel, crab, and stem counts are referencing a 1/16 meter squared plot.For ease of comparison, I am going to extrapolate it to a meter square density
```{r meter-squared}
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(
    Live_count1 = Live_count1*16,
    Dead_count1 = Dead_count1*16,
    Mussel_count = Mussel_count*16,
    Burrow_count = Burrow_count*16, 
    Live_count2 = Live_count2*16,
    Dead_count2 = Dead_count2*16, 
    Crabf = factor(Crab),
    Musself = factor(Mussel),
    Treatmentf = factor(Treatment),
    Site_IDF = factor(Site_ID),
    Replicatef = factor(Replicate)) %>%
  mutate(
    Category = case_when(
      Crab == "yes" & Mussel == "no" ~ "Crab",
      Crab == "no" & Mussel == "yes" ~ "Mussel",
      Crab == "yes" & Mussel == "yes" ~ "Crab + Mussel",
      TRUE ~ "None"
    )
  )

print(dat)

ss_dat <- ss_dat %>% #need these as factors for making models later
  mutate(
   Crabf = factor(Crab),
    Musself = factor(Mussel),
    Treatmentf = factor(Treatment),
    Site_IDF = factor(Site_ID)
  )

```

Complete summary stats for soil strength data by gaining means, sd, min, and max for each treatment and depth
```{r ss summary}

summary_ss <- ss_dat %>% #get means for simplicity of the plot
  group_by(Treatment, Vane_depth) %>%
  summarise(mean = mean(Strength), 
            se = sd(Strength),
            xmin = mean - se,
            xmax = mean + se,
            .groups = "drop")%>%
  mutate(Treatment = dplyr::recode(Treatment,
    "cc" = "Crab Only",
    "mc" = "Mussel Only",
    "mcc" = "Crab & Mussel",
    "ncnc" = "Reference",
    "ncnm" = "Control"
  ))

print(summary_ss)
```

Combining Sediment deposition dat with main data table 
```{r}
new_dat <- left_join(dat, sed_dat, by = "Site_ID")
```

###Control to Reference Plot Comparisons
H0: Control plots are not different than reference plots for sediment depoistion or soil strength

If I fail to reject the null hypothesis I can remove reference plot treatments from my modeling analysis as there was no effect of the caging material on my desired response variables. 
```{r Mann-Whitney U, t-test}
#Sediment Deposition comparison test first
dat2 <- new_dat%>%
  filter(Treatment %in% c("ncnc", "ncnm"))

##Normality check 
ggplot(dat2,aes(x = sed_av)) + 
  geom_histogram() + 
  stat_bin(bins = 10)+
  theme_classic()

qqnorm(dat2$sed_av)
qqline(dat2$sed_av, lwd = 2, col = "blue") #slight right skew 

##test
shapiro.test(dat2$sed_av) #W = 0.89459, p-value = 0.06588, data is normal so I can use t-test

t.test(sed_av ~ Treatment, data = dat2) #t = 0.13405, df = 10.797, p-value = 0.8958, so I fail to reject the null hypothesis

#Soil Strength Comparison test, have to check at each depth interval to compare the two groups 

##depth 0-10cm
###Normality check
qqnorm(dat2$ss1)
qqline(dat2$ss1, lwd = 2, col = "blue") #dip in the middle  

shapiro.test(dat2$ss1) #W = 0.92816, p-value = 0.2279, data is normal so can use the two sample t-test

##test
t.test(ss1 ~ Treatment, data = dat2) #t = 1.1035, df = 12.098, p-value = 0.2913

##depth 10-20cm
###Normality check
qqnorm(dat2$ss2)
qqline(dat2$ss2, lwd = 2, col = "blue") #looks good 

shapiro.test(dat2$ss2) #W = 0.9652, p-value = 0.7561, data is normal so can use the two sample t-test
##test
t.test(ss2 ~ Treatment, data = dat2) #t = 1.39, df = 12.512, p-value = 0.1888

##depth 20-30cm
###Normality check
qqnorm(dat2$ss3)
qqline(dat2$ss3, lwd = 2, col = "blue") #looks good 

shapiro.test(dat2$ss3) #W = 0.98522, p-value = 0.9917, data is normal so can use the two sample t-test

##test
t.test(ss3 ~ Treatment, data = dat2) #t = 0.69953, df = 13.995, p-value = 0.4957

##depth 30-40cm
###Normality check
qqnorm(dat2$ss4)
qqline(dat2$ss4, lwd = 2, col = "blue") #slight deviations at end points

shapiro.test(dat2$ss4) #W = 0.98007, p-value = 0.9642, data is normal so can use the two sample t-test

##test
t.test(ss4 ~ Treatment, data = dat2) #t = -0.38713, df = 12.821, p-value = 0.705

##depth 40-50cm
###Normality check
qqnorm(dat2$ss5)
qqline(dat2$ss5, lwd = 2, col = "blue") #slight deviations at end points

shapiro.test(dat2$ss5) #W = 0.92715, p-value = 0.2196, data is normal so can use the two sample t-test

##test
t.test(ss5 ~ Treatment, data = dat2) #t = -0.15377, df = 13.295, p-value = 0.8801

#Bonferroni adjustment
##because I did 6 statistical tests with these two treatments I need to correct my p-value to alpha/number of tests which the new alpha would be 0.0083. This shouldn't be a problem because I am hoping for the null hypothesis
```
Conclusions: Based on the two sample t-tests conducted and the Mann Whitney-U test, the control and references cages are not different in terms of the two response variables: sediment deposition and soil strength. Thus, I can remove reference cages from analysis when considering my models and just have the controls against the other treatments. 

#Models 
##Q1
1.How does the presence of the fiddler crab, Minuca pugnax, effect salt marsh stability: resistance to erosion (quantified by soil strength as a proxy) and vertical accretion?

I am going to start with a general linear model even though we are dealing with continuous all positive data as a starting point. Because the data is continuous with positive values I will use a gamma distribution with an inverse canonical link or a lognormal to see if that will fit the data better. I will make models with replicate as a random variable to deal with the cages not being truly independent from each other due to proximity of all of the cages being in one site. As well as set elevation as a fixed effect for some of the models. 
```{r model}
#make new dataset without the reference plots
dat3 <- new_dat %>%
  filter(Treatment %in% c("cc", "ncnm", "mc", "mcc"))%>%
  mutate(
    Treatment = dplyr::recode(
      Treatment,
      "cc" = "Crab Only",
      "mc" = "Mussel Only",
      "mcc" = "Mussel & Crab",
      "ncnm" = "Control"
    ) )%>%
      mutate(
    Treatmentf = dplyr::recode(
      Treatmentf,
      "cc" = "Crab Only",
      "mc" = "Mussel Only",
      "mcc" = "Mussel & Crab",
      "ncnm" = "Control"
    )
  )

hist(dat3$sed_av)

#check for multicolinearity
GGally::ggpairs(dat3[,c(15, 29, 45)]) #not straight lines, so we are looking good here

#potential models

m0a <- lm(sed_av ~ Treatmentf, data = dat3)
summary(m0a)#The standard errors look good as they are all an order of magnitude lower. The mussel crab cage and reference cage has a lower sediment deposition compared to the crab cage. The mussel cage has a higher sediment deposition compared to the crab cage. Multiple r squared is low (o.o4195), this currently doesn't really describe what's happening.
check_model(m0a)#Normality looks a little skewed at the extremes but nothing I am too worried about. The homogeneity of variance however, could be better so I am going to compared with a GLM

m1a <- lm(sed_av ~ Treatmentf*Elevation, data = dat3)
summary(m1a)

m2a <- lmer(sed_av ~ Treatmentf*Elevation + (1|Replicatef), data = dat3)
summary(m2a)

m0b <- glmmTMB(sed_av ~ Treatmentf, data = dat3, family = Gamma(link = "log"))
summary(m0b) #The standard error is high compared to the estimates. The estimates for all other treatments compared to cc is the same, which seems off

check_model(m0b)

m0c <- glmmTMB(sed_av ~ Treatmentf, data = dat3, family = lognormal())
summary(m0c)

check_model(m0c) #lognormal distribution looks better based on check models

m1 <- glmmTMB(sed_av ~ Treatmentf + Elevation, data = dat3, family = lognormal())
summary(m1)#standard errors are not better as they are still on the same order of magnitude, the elevation error is an order of magnitude less than estimate

m2 <- glmmTMB(sed_av ~ Treatmentf + Elevation + (1|Replicatef), data = dat3, family = lognormal())
summary(m2) #random effect standard error is higher than variance. 

m3 <-glmmTMB(sed_av ~ Treatmentf + Elevation + Live_count2, data = dat3, family = lognormal())
summary(m3)#Standard errors are still on the same order of magnitude for some values

m4 <-glmmTMB(sed_av ~ Treatmentf*Live_count2 + Elevation*Live_count2, data = dat3, family = lognormal())
summary(m4)

m5 <-glmmTMB(sed_av ~ Treatmentf*Live_count2 + Elevation*Live_count2 + (1|Replicate), data = dat3, family = lognormal())
summary(m5)

m6 <-glmmTMB(sed_av ~ Treatmentf + Elevation + Live_count2 + (1|Replicatef), data = dat3, family = lognormal())
summary(m6)

```
###Model Selection
```{r AIC}

AIC(m0a, m0b, m0c, m1, m2, m3, m4, m5, m6) %>%
  arrange(AIC) %>%
  print()

#m6 had the lowest AIC at -138

```

###Diagnostic plots to check model assumptions
```{r, check_model}

performance::check_model(m6)
check_overdispersion(m6) #no overdispersion detected so that is not why the variance is not spread evenly
#Homogeneity of variance is not the best however, I think because of how variable this data is, that is why we are seeing issues with linearity. 
```

###Model Predictions
```{r}
# use the ggpredict function in the ggeffects package to get estimated adjusted predictions and confidence intervals for each species at different levels of species

m6_ggpredict <- 
  ggeffects::ggpredict(m6, terms = c("Treatmentf"))

print(m6_ggpredict, n = Inf)

test_predictions(m6_ggpredict) #none of the treatments were statistically significant from each other

plot(m6_ggpredict) # default interaction plot

#make a better plot 
m6_fig <- ggplot(m6_ggpredict, aes(x = x, y = predicted))+
  geom_point(size = 3, show.legend = FALSE)+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high), width = 0.2)+
  geom_point(data = dat3, aes(x = Treatmentf, y = sed_av, color = Treatment), inherit.aes = FALSE, show.legend = FALSE)+ 
  labs(
    x = "Treatment",
    y = bquote("Sediment Deposition"~(g~cm^{-2}~yr^{-1}))
    )+
  theme(legend.position = "none")+
  theme_classic()

print(m6_fig)
```
